_comment: XSOAR list — imported via Settings → Advanced → Lists → New. Format: 'JSON' content type. Source of truth: mappings/mitre-attack-enterprise/tlctc-enterprise-attack.json. Regenerate from the source mapping when ATT&CK ships an upstream update (typically twice yearly).
_format: Each key is an ATT&CK technique ID. Value is { primary, sequence, splits } where 'sequence' is the canonical step sequence per TLCTC rules and 'splits' explains why a single technique fires multiple cluster playbooks.
_excerpt: Top 60 entries — full list (~698 techniques) is generated from the mapping file. Edit the source mapping, not this file.

T1001.splits: Direct #7 if foreign binary; #1→#7 if LOLBAS like certutil/PowerShell

T1003.splits: OS credential dumping via legitimate API → #1 Abuse of Functions; the credential APPLICATION is a separate #4 step (R-CRED)

T1003.001.splits: comsvcs.dll MiniDump is a designed Windows function — #1. Credential use later = #4 (R-CRED)

T1003.002.splits: SAM hive read via legitimate API

T1003.003.splits: NTDS dit access via legitimate API

T1018.splits: Remote system discovery using built-in tools

T1021.splits: Remote services authenticated with valid credentials → #4 (R-CRED)

T1027.splits: Obfuscated payload — payload is FEC; obfuscation does not change cluster

T1036.splits: Masquerading targets human/system trust → #9 if human-targeted

T1041.splits: Exfil over C2 channel using designed network functions

T1055.splits: Process injection: API abuse (#1) + injected code execution (#7) per Axiom VI + R-EXEC

T1059.splits: Interpreter is #1; the executed script is #7 (R-EXEC). Both steps required.

T1068.splits: Privilege escalation via OS/kernel flaw exploitation → #2 (server-role under R-ROLE: kernel as service to user-mode code)

T1078.splits: Valid Accounts — credential application is ALWAYS #4 regardless of how creds were obtained (R-CRED)

T1083.splits: File and Directory Discovery via designed APIs

T1098.splits: Account manipulation — designed admin function abused (post-auth #4 typically precedes)

T1110.splits: Brute force — guessing credentials → #4 (cred acquisition + application)

T1133.splits: External Remote Services authenticated with creds → #4. Service exposure itself is #1-context.

T1189.splits: Drive-by Compromise: exploits flaw in victim's CLIENT (browser) under R-ROLE → #3

T1190.splits: Public-Facing Application: exploits flaw in SERVER → #2 (R-ROLE)

T1195.splits: Supply Chain Compromise: #10 placed at Trust Acceptance Event (R-SUPPLY)

T1195.001.splits: Software dependency compromise — TAE at install/update

T1199.splits: Trusted relationship — TAE when partner trust is accepted

T1203.splits: Exploitation for Client Execution: client-role flaw → #3

T1210.splits: Exploitation of Remote Services: remote service is server-role → #2

T1219.splits: Remote access tool deployed via social engineering typically — split per Axiom VI

T1486.splits: Data Encrypted for Impact (ransomware): payload execution = #7. Outcome [DRE: Ac] — accessibility loss.

T1496.splits: Resource hijacking — abuse of compute capacity

T1505.splits: Server software component — abuse of designed extension mechanism

T1505.003.splits: Web shell installed via designed extension point

T1547.splits: Boot or logon autostart — designed extension abused

T1555.splits: Credentials from password stores — #1 acquisition; subsequent USE = #4

T1562.splits: Impair defenses — abuse of admin functions to disable controls

T1566.splits: Phishing — #9 lure step. Payload execution is a SEPARATE step (#3 or #7 depending on attachment vs link, R-EXEC).

T1566.001.splits: Spearphishing Attachment: #9 lure + #7 if FEC executes (R-EXEC). Both steps required per Axiom VI.

T1566.002.splits: Spearphishing Link — #9 lure; if click leads to browser exploit add #3, if download+execute add #7

T1566.003.splits: Spearphishing via service — same as T1566.001/.002 depending on follow-on

T1567.splits: Exfiltration over web service — abuse of designed channel

T1574.002.splits: DLL side-loading — abuse of designed loader behavior
